title: Finite periodic Q3 split Gibbs/KMS source and shape stress
question: On the registered finite periodic-control graphs (bond2, square4 and grid2x3), do all source sites retain the finite Gibbs stationarity and analytic KMS mesh-decrease pattern for both split orders, signs and beta values, and how does the residual change with graph degree and shape?
method: Reconstruct the manifest-defined d=3 Q3 onsite quartic and nonlinear bond matrices on bond2, square4 and grid2x3 with chi=1, r=-1, g=3/5, c=3/5 and lambda=1/10; validate edge bounds, uniqueness and all-site source coverage.
At every declared source site, use A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar) and B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar), the exact finite-H Gibbs state at beta=0.25 and 0.5, and the KMS boundary t+i beta hbar with horizon t=0.1.

Evaluate onsite-then-manifest-bonds and reverse-term split products at delta=0.1 and 0.05 for both real-time signs. Build each complex inverse with reverse factor order and -z, and retain trace-norm Gibbs stationarity defects and scalar KMS residuals.

Require exact-H controls below 1e-9, positive finite split witnesses, all-source coverage, per-source coarse/fine decrease and shape/degree summaries; treat the two-mesh ratios as finite diagnostics rather than analytic uniform constants.

Run a non-importing independent reconstruction and an integrated verifier comparing all 192 source rows, 48 exact rows, 96 mesh rows, 12 source summaries, 3 shape summaries, provenance hashes, Lean R247 and scope firewalls.
finding: Primary 930/930 and independent 929/929 assertions pass over 192 finite source/order/sign/beta/mesh rows, with 48 exact controls, 96 mesh rows, 12 source sites and 3 graph shapes; the integrated verifier passes 40/40 with Lean R247 PASS. The maximum primary-independent discrepancy over stationarity, KMS and inverse-error fields is 8.906604324797492e-13. Across all rows the KMS residual ranges from 9.203548117557915e-05 to 0.02045220126762285 and the stationarity defect from 0.0006767190119555736 to 0.014182652533020666. Every source context decreases from delta=0.1 to 0.05; KMS fine/coarse ratios range from 0.4267810916211172 to 0.6709540230112263 and stationarity ratios from 0.49891203239653653 to 0.49990755630506695. Shape maxima increase from bond2 KMS 0.002642760989279424 to square4 0.008505633932616146 to grid2x3 0.02045220126762285; degree-three grid sources reach about 0.02045 while degree-two grid sources reach about 0.00812. The finite pattern is reproducible, but the degree/shape dependence is a concrete warning against treating this as a source- or volume-uniform rate.
decision_reason: This extends the finite Q3 equilibrium-interface diagnostic from path exhaustions to explicit periodic-control shapes and makes graph degree dependence visible. It is useful QFT-facing evidence for targeting a weighted common-core/Trotter estimate, while the observed finite mesh decrease cannot replace a direct D/delta-D Cauchy bound uniform in source, volume, cutoff and beta. The graph set is finite and does not establish arbitrary-shape exhaustion independence or a thermodynamic torus dynamics.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 periodic-control Q3 KMS diagnostic. It is not a thermodynamic-limit source-uniformity theorem, a common-alpha construction, an OS/KMS identification, a mass-gap proof, a continuum result, or a QFT/Clay closure.

qft_interface.closed: Exact finite-H Gibbs controls and source-wise split stationarity/KMS residuals are reproduced on every site of the manifest-defined bond2, square4 and grid2x3 controls for both split orders, signs, beta values and meshes; finite degree/shape summaries are recorded.
qft_interface.open: A source-, volume-, cutoff- and beta-uniform analytic rate, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common unbounded core, arbitrary-shape exhaustion independence, one common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS quotient, GNS gap, continuum and physical TECT gates remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

adversarial_review.check: The three explicit manifest edge sets and all source sites are checked; the controls are not labelled an infinite periodic torus or thermodynamic limit.
The alpha convention uses t+i beta hbar at every source and both real-time signs with hbar=1; exact-H controls are checked before split residuals.
Complex products use reverse factor order and -z for their inverse, not a complex adjoint shortcut; inverse errors are asserted for every graph/order/mesh/sign/beta row.
Only d=3 is admitted and a positive [H,H_onsite] witness is required for every graph; the commuting d=2 degeneration is excluded.
All finite sites are measured and degree-three versus degree-two variation is reported; no source-uniform direct Cauchy or limiting bound is inferred.
Per-source coarse/fine decreases are checked on two mesh values only; their ratios are not promoted to a uniform analytic Trotter rate.
Bond2, square4 and grid2x3 expose finite degree/shape dependence; three finite controls do not establish arbitrary-shape exhaustion independence.
The independent lane rebuilds oscillator tensors, periodic bond terms and residuals without importing the primary; the maximum numerical discrepancy is below 9e-13.
R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation and conditional-transfer scope; dense periodic matrices and all limiting interfaces remain Python evidence/open analysis.
Finite periodic controls do not prove a common core, direct Cauchy convergence, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

next_action: Use the degree/shape residual range to target a periodic common-core estimate with explicit degree constants and a direct D/delta-D Cauchy comparison across increasing controls; if those constants grow with cutoff, volume or degree, record the route-local obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
no_overclaim: This package proves only finite d=3 matrix identities and diagnostics. It does not prove a source-uniform thermodynamic Q3 dynamics, common alpha, OS/KMS identification, a mass gap, continuum removal, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or a Clay result.
